messages:
alex: Heads up — ruby sampleapp streaming chat with structured output (function-calls) is producing chunk boundaries that split JSON objects. client-side JSON.parse crashes. repro below. :frowning:

maria: can you paste a minimal repro and lib versions?

alex: sure, minimal snippet i used (ruby 3.2, ruby-sdk 0.9.3):
```ruby
resp = Client.chat.stream(prompt: '...')
resp.each do |chunk|
  # chunk is a raw transport piece, often like '{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"foo\":'
  json = JSON.parse(chunk) # <-- raises on partial data
end
```

sam: this matches what i expect at the transport layer — TCP/chunking can split logical messages. go-sdk assembles framing and yields complete JSON events; ruby currently yields raw bytes.

nate: we landed SSE-style framing in go-sdk (emits complete json per event) — see PR that switched stream -> ndjson/sse. we should mirror for parity.

julia: quick proposal: add a `streaming_framing: :ndjson` option to Client#chat.stream that assembles until newline-delimited JSON and yields whole objects. default nil to preserve current behaviour. deprecate old behavior in next major.

alex: i can open the issue + PR. plan: buffer incoming chunks, append until we can parse a full JSON object (or until a newline delimiter), then yield the parsed event. will add unit tests simulating partial chunks. any objections to opt-in framing first?

maria: no objections. keep default unchanged for now, add opt-in flag + changelog note. tests should include mixed boundaries (multiple objects in one chunk, single object split across many).

ci-bot: CI: ruby-integration-suite failed on ruby_stream_parsing_spec (flake) — job logs: https://ci.redwood/internal/12345

nate: sgtm. if you want, copy the small assembler from go-sdk and adapt to ruby. it's ~40 lines.

alex: opening issue now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sdk/issues/456. assigning to self, will post PR tomorrow with tests.

julia: :thumbsup: i'll review the PR. thanks for taking this on.
